title: Refunds and Credit Balances: Hospital Account (Encounter Billing) Policy
content:
A credit balance (a negative patient balance) arises on a Hospital Account (Encounter Billing) account when payments exceed what the patient owes after later adjustments.

## Clauses

1. The credit is first offset against the patient's other patient-due accounts under the payment-application rule.
2. The remaining credit is refunded only when it is at least the refund minimum, within the refund issue days, in calendar days, of the date the credit arose.
3. The refund is booked against the payment that created the credit, most recent payment first, never refunding more than that payment's amount.
4. A payment is refunded at most once.
5. The refund goes back to the original card when the source payment was a card payment posted no more than the card-refund age limit in calendar days before the refund date, by ACH credit when the source was an ACH bank draft, and by paper check otherwise.
6. A credit below the refund minimum stays on the profile and offsets the patient's next liability.

## Worked illustration (hypothetical payments)

An account shows a credit of 150.00 after an adjustment. The patient's two payments on it were 100.00 (most recent) and 300.00. With no other patient-due account to offset, the refund books 100.00 against the most recent payment and the remaining 50.00 against the earlier one; neither payment is refunded again.
